cells.tense: You are tending what's yours right now, and the tending is holding.
cells.act: accept the acknowledgment when it comes
cells.ask: When thanks comes your way, don't wave it off. Let it land, say you're glad it helped, keep the rest short. One sentence is enough, then back to what you were doing.
cells.core:
What you're caring for is in good shape, and yours are the hands doing the caring. You add when it needs adding, step back when it doesn't, and you can feel in your hands where care ends and grip starts. Somewhere in all of it you're giving something up to keep this going, and the people it's for can see that, even if nobody says so out loud.

So let them say so. When the thanks comes, take it in instead of batting it down. Say you're glad it helped and stop there. Then go back to it. Do this once and notice what happens when you don't deflect it — the loop closes, and a closed loop is what lets you set something down later without feeling it went unseen.
cells.sheetLine: Let the thanks land once, then go back to it.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with your own hands, on purpose
cells.place: a place where you keep adjusting the mix — adding here, taking away there — so the whole thing keeps moving

cells.tense: You are bracing for a version of this that hasn't arrived yet and can't be written in from here.
cells.act: walk through the thing you built and touch nothing
cells.ask: Go through what you've made with your hands behind your back. No fixing, no straightening, no noting what's next. Look at what's finished, then walk out.
cells.core:
You're out past the work. Planning what comes after the next stage before the current one has had its hour, because the hour looks small compared to what might go wrong. That's care, and it's also a hand that doesn't know how to stop, and what you're tending can feel the hand hovering over it. The adjusting has stopped responding to the mix and started responding to the future.

So walk through what you've made and touch nothing. Go through it, hands off, fifteen minutes. Not to fix it or spot the next move — to be in it as it is. What's done is allowed to be done. You're keeping your balance while you're still here rather than already at the next thing, and the next thing will still be there when you come back to it.
cells.sheetLine: Go through what's finished and don't touch it.
cells.verb: tending what's growing with your own hands, on purpose
cells.place: a place where you keep adjusting the mix — adding here, taking away there — so the whole thing keeps moving

cells.tense: You walked through this particular door a long time ago and you're still standing at it.
cells.act: keep following the star after everything that has happened
cells.ask: Name what you set out toward, before everything that happened, and give it fifteen minutes sometime soon. Not a plan, not catching up — the work itself. Once, then let the week go on.
cells.core:
The care is there but the fuel isn't. You're still doing what a person who tends things does — showing up, covering what needs covering — but the adjusting has gone mechanical, motion without the mix responding. Before the door you walked through, there was a direction you picked for yourself, and that direction isn't in your hands the way it used to be.

So follow that direction one more week. Pick the thing you set out toward, before everything that happened, and give it fifteen minutes. Not a review or a plan, the work itself, once, small. You're not trying to feel it again; you're giving tested hope one more week to stand on. Whether the feeling comes back is not yours to schedule — it can arrive in its own time, on top of the work.
cells.sheetLine: You're still here. Give the old hope one small week.

cells.tense: You're doing the tending that holds this together and you'd say nobody is doing it, it just runs.
cells.act: do the giving in the open this time, where it was always done unseen
cells.ask: Do a piece of it this week where one person can watch you do it. Not the finished result — the doing. Keep it plain, and don't explain it after.
cells.core:
You're holding the balance here and the account you keep doesn't include you. When something gets covered or adjusted, your version is that it needed doing and it got done. There's a hand on all of this, and it's yours, and your account of it keeps leaving the hand out. Others may have noticed; you'd say they haven't, or that it's nothing.

So this week, do one piece where it can be seen. Not the finished thing — the act itself, small, in front of the person it's for. No speech after, no 'it was nothing' to close it off. Just let it be what it is, with a witness. What's yours stays yours after it's been seen. That's the whole change, and it asks nothing of you but being visible for a minute.

The asks survive being wrong because they are single small acts drawn from the medicine's own list — an hour with a finished thing, a walk through something built, a star followed another week — each useful even if the status diagnosis is off.
